title: Pawprint connector catalog
description: Upstream-owned catalog of connectors, their permission tiers, and the capabilities each tier unlocks. Adopters do not edit this file; they choose which connectors to enable, and at which tier, in their own deploy.config.json.

capabilities.description: What Pawprint can do once a connector is connected. A capability with unmet requirements is unavailable and must say why, rather than failing at the point of use.

identity.description: Which identity system governs this connector.

detect.description: How the wizard detects whether this environment is present, before asking for anything.

probe.description: Read-only probe. Must never require a permission beyond what sign-in already grants.

tiers.description: Ordered from least to most privileged. An adopter picks the lowest tier that unlocks what they need.

consent.description: user: the signed-in user can consent for themselves. admin: a directory admin must consent for the organisation. none: no consent step exists.

reversible.description: False where granting cannot be cleanly undone, which must be surfaced before the grant is requested.

name.description: Permission name as the provider defines it. Resolved to an identifier at runtime rather than hardcoded, so a rename upstream surfaces as a clear error instead of a wrong grant.

type.description: delegated: acts as the signed-in user and can never exceed their access. application: standing access independent of any user, and therefore a larger grant.

scope.description: For azure-role, the narrowest scope the role is assigned at.

rationale.description: Why this permission is needed. A permission without a stated reason does not belong in the catalog.

degraded.description: What Pawprint does when the requirement is unmet. Stating this forces every capability to fail gracefully rather than at the point of use.
